messages:
alex: Heads up — ran into a messy ESM/CJS/edge compatibility issue while wiring the JS SDK for a sample app. Node 18+ has global fetch, but our CI (Node16) and customers on Vercel Edge / Cloudflare behave differently. Which approach should we recommend in docs: always ship undici and polyfill, or prefer globalThis.fetch when present and fallback to undici?

maya: prefer runtime-detection + minimal fallback. docs should show a tiny runtime-agnostic wrapper. keeps bundle small for edge where global fetch exists. :+1:

sam: agreed. also call out differences: undici fetch supports Agent keepAlive / connection pooling (Node), but edge runtimes ignore Agent options. so our retry/timeout behavior must be conservative in edge.

jin: +1. we should add a checklist for authors of sample apps: (1) test in Node16, Node18, Bun, Vercel Edge, Cloudflare Workers; (2) ensure auth headers are attached before retries; (3) don't rely on Agent options in edge.

maya: here's the wrapper snippet we used in the SDK (ESM-friendly):

```
// runtime-fetch.ts (ESM)
export const getFetch = async () => {
  if (typeof globalThis.fetch === 'function') return globalThis.fetch;
  // dynamic import to avoid importing undici in edge bundles
  const { fetch } = await import('undici');
  return fetch;
};
```

maya: Notes: 1) This uses dynamic import so bundlers that target edge won't include undici. 2) For CJS consumers we ship a small shim that does `module.exports = require('./cjs-runtime-fetch')` with the equivalent require-based fallback.

alex: what about TypeScript types? we should export a FetchLike type so apps can type wrappers.

maya: yes — something like:

```
export type FetchLike = (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>;
export declare function getFetch(): Promise<FetchLike>;
```

sam: add guidance for polyfills in examples: Node <18 CI (or older customers) can do: `globalThis.fetch = (await import('undici')).fetch;` in their test bootstrap. For CJS test bootstrap: `globalThis.fetch = require('undici').fetch;`

jin: also mention stream/body differences: Cloudflare/Workers use Web Streams for response.body, Node's undici uses Node streams unless you use the WHATWG Response. Might need response.clone() in retry logic.

maya: good call. For retry behavior we should: 1) only retry idempotent requests by default (GET, HEAD); 2) let callers opt-in for retries on POST with a deduplication key; 3) ensure auth headers are re-attached before retry (bearer tokens sometimes consumed by interceptors).

alex: how to document bundling/entry points for ESM/CJS? a lot of users stumble over `require()` failing against an ESM-only package.

maya: recommend dual entrypoints in package.json: "exports": { ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js" } } and ship types at `./dist/esm/index.d.ts`. Also include a small README snippet: if you need CJS in older apps, use the cjs entrypoint.

sam: one more gotcha: tree-shaking and top-level await. Avoid TLA in entrypoints that import undici — keep dynamic import inside a function so bundlers can drop it.

ops-bot: deploy-bot detected new sample-app PR touching sdk bootstrap. CI matrix: node16, node18, bun, vercel-edge, cloudflare-workers.

jin: can we add a tiny section to onboarding docs titled "Fetch polyfill & runtimes" with the wrapper, the TS types, and the bullet checklist? I can take it if folks 👍

alex: please do. include the code snippets and a one-paragraph note on why undici is only a fallback. also add the auth/retry recommendations and a short table of runtime capabilities (Agent, keepAlive, WHATWG streams).

maya: I'll paste a minimal table for that doc in the PR. rough: Node+undici = Agent yes, WHATWG: partial; Node18 native = Agent yes, WHATWG yes; Vercel Edge = Agent no, WHATWG yes; CF Workers = Agent no, WHATWG yes; Bun = partial Agent, WHATWG yes.

alex: perfect. thanks — this should cut down on onboarding friction. :tada:

maya: will open a docs PR and a sample-app PR that demonstrates both patterns (explicit polyfill + pure edge).

sam: leaving a note to QA: when testing, verify auth + retry behavior by running a flaky stub server that drops connections on first try.

jin: thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
